cards.explanation: The answer is the town nearest the body. The elders and judges measure from the victim to the neighboring cities, and then the elders of the city nearest the victim take the heifer (Deuteronomy 21:2-3). Nobody gets to say "not my town." The measuring tape settles it, friends.

The answer is that God chose the priests to serve and rule on cases. Moses says the priests, the sons of Levi, come forward because "…the LORD your God has chosen them to serve Him and pronounce blessings in His name and to give a ruling in every dispute and case of assault." They aren't there by accident, friends. God picked them for this.

The answer is False. The elders declare, "Our hands did not shed this blood, nor did our eyes see it." They say it out loud, standing at the stream with their hands washed over the heifer. So they don't claim to have seen who killed the man. Say it with me, friends: their eyes did not see it.

The answer is True. Right after the elders pray, "Accept this atonement, O LORD, for Your people Israel whom You have redeemed…" Moses says, "And the bloodshed will be atoned for." That's the promise of the passage, friends (Deuteronomy 21:8). It's settled.
The answer is guilt. Moses says, "So you shall purge from among you the guilt of shedding innocent blood…" The innocent blood is why this whole ceremony exists, friends.
The answer is True. Moses says, "…since you have done what is right in the eyes of the LORD." Israel follows the steps, and the LORD sees it as right. That's a good word to hear, friends.

The answer is False. Moses says, "…you are to let her go wherever she wishes. But you must not sell her for money or treat her as a slave…" Heavy topic, friends, but the text is clear that she isn't to be sold.

The answer is that he has dishonored her. Moses says the man must not sell her or treat her as a slave, "…since you have dishonored her." That's the reason the text gives, friends, and I won't add a thing to it.

The answer is True. Moses says the father "…must not appoint the son of the beloved wife as the firstborn over the son of the unloved wife." He must acknowledge the firstborn, the unloved wife's son. Who the father loves more doesn't change who came first, friends.

The answer is a double portion of all he has. Moses says the father must acknowledge the firstborn "…by giving him a double portion of all that he has." That son belongs to the wife called unloved, and the father can't slide the firstborn's right over to the favorite's son (Deuteronomy 21:15–16). I think that's one family meeting where nobody gets to say "but I'm the favorite," friends. The text says the right of the firstborn belongs to him, and that's the end of the discussion.

The answer is that he's the first son born of his father's strength. Moses says, "For that son is the firstfruits of his father’s strength; the right of the firstborn belongs to him." The reason is that he's the first son, friends, not who his mother is.

The answer is that he is a glutton and a drunkard. The parents tell the elders, "This son of ours is stubborn and rebellious; he does not obey us. He is a glutton and a drunkard." It's a heavy section, friends, so I'll just say that plainly and move on.
The answer is evil. Moses says, "So you must purge the evil from among you, and all Israel will hear and be afraid." It's a heavy line, friends, and the word fits it.
The answer is False. Moses says, "…all Israel will hear and be afraid." The word spreads, friends, which is the opposite of keeping it quiet.

The answer is to bury it that same day. Moses says, "…you must not leave the body on the tree overnight, but you must be sure to bury him that day…" No overnight stay is allowed, friends. Moses also says the land is something the LORD is giving them as an inheritance, and they must not defile it (Deuteronomy 21:23).

The answer is curse. Moses says, "…because anyone who is hung on a tree is under God’s curse." That's why the body can't stay up overnight, friends. It's a solemn line, and I'll leave it as the text gives it.
